stem.text: Let \( f(x) = -\left(\sqrt[5]{x - 3}\right)^{7} + 4 \). Determine whether f is differentiable at \( x = 3 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is differentiable at \( x = 3 \) with \( f'(3) = 0 \), because the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides.

worked_solution.text: f is continuous at \( x = 3 \), since \( f(3) = 4 \) and the root is continuous everywhere.
The difference quotient is \( \frac{f(3 + h) - f(3)}{h} = -h^{\frac{2}{5}} \), and the exponent \( \frac{2}{5} \) is positive.
So the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides, f is differentiable at \( x = 3 \), and \( f'(3) = 0 \). The tangent line there is horizontal.

options.label: f is not differentiable at \( x = 3 \), because \( f'(x) = - \frac{7}{5}\left(\sqrt[5]{x - 3}\right)^{2} \) is 0 there, so the tangent is vertical.
options.derivation: a zero derivative read as a vertical tangent instead of a horizontal one
